annotationRationale: Finite geometric sums encode the repeated digits. Subtracting equations for two lengths forces coefficient conditions, and the integer digit restrictions leave an exhaustive list of triples.
sourceMethod: Follows the official geometric-sum representation and subtraction of the equations for two distinct values of n. Makes the cancellation and the sufficiency of the surviving triples explicit.

review.mathCheck: Since n>0, cancellation of 10^n−1 is valid. Two distinct lengths force 9c=a² and b=2c. The nonzero digit restriction leaves exactly (3,2,1) and (6,8,4); both satisfy the original equation for every positive n. Their sums are 6 and 18, so D is correct.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded, faithful adaptation of official solution #25 on pages 15–16: encode repdigits by geometric sums, subtract the two length equations, and exhaust the digit possibilities. The candidate explicitly verifies sufficiency through reversible transformations.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed integer restrictions and geometric-sum representation are central to the solution. Subtraction elimination is appropriate supporting knowledge. No material omission or incorrect direct node.
